analysis.title: The Flow Show: DEM fatale
key_insights: BofA stays risk-off until central bank rate hikes end (41 in the past 6 months), the 10-year UST yield falls below 4.5% and oil falls below $80/bbl, which it says is needed to reverse the tightening of financial conditions.
If November CPI and payrolls are weak, BofA says the December Fed/ECB/BoJ hikes would be the last, and risk assets would start a year-end rally around Thanksgiving.
BofA flags a 'double-top' in the S&P 500 Equal-Weighted Index (SPW) and says no one is talking about a 'big top'.

NDX is down 15% over the past month. NVDA is below $200, TSM below $400 and MAGS below $70. BofA says SPX holds above 7,000 and risk rotates (tech bonds, Europe, China, consumer) as long as recession odds stay low (banks IXG hold $125, mid-caps MDY $666, junk bonds JNK $92).

BofA recommends buying gold ahead of the debt ceiling. Congress is sworn in Jan 3 and US debt hits the $41.1tn ceiling around Feb 1 on the current 12-month run rate. Gold rose 12% and 17% in the 3 months before the 2011 and 2023 debt-ceiling standoffs.

BofA reads the Democratic midterm result as a shift from populist capitalism to populist socialism, with taxes and regulation going up (negative for EPS). It says this signals gold over oil, lower yields, tech bonds over tech stocks, consumer stocks over energy, small caps over monopolies, and long Europe and China tech.
BofA says the 2026 midterms mark peak AI equity concentration.
Hyperscaler capex consensus is $239bn in 2024, $412bn in 2025, $820bn in 2026 and $1.3tn in 2027. Free cash flow is $191bn in 2025, -$63bn in 2026 and -$252bn in 2027.

AI funding has shifted to external capital. Global debt issuance is $297bn YTD versus $110bn in 2025, and equity issuance is $100bn YTD versus $4bn in 2025. Buybacks are $14bn YTD annualized versus $90bn in 2025.

BofA says bond and credit markets want AI capex and issuance to slow, which would favour MAGS 'spenders' over AI 'builders' such as semis and neoclouds. AI stocks return once yields reset lower without a recession.
Data centers are electorally unpopular, and many incoming Democratic governors campaigned on stopping them. BofA says its 2028 AI capex forecast of about $2tn is probably a little too high.

The Fed hiked on Sep 16. Markets price a 64% chance of another hike on Dec 9, 76% for the ECB and 50% for the BOE on Dec 17, and 68% for the BOJ on Dec 18. There have been 55 rate hikes this year against 11 expected in January.

BofA says oil needs to fall sharply for the tightening cycle to end before a credit event or recession. Its stance is sell energy, buy consumer, sell oil, buy bonds, and wait for lower oil and yields before adding risk 'bigtime'.

BofA's 2027 scenarios are bubble, breadth and bust. It says consensus conviction in the bubble case (50% of Oct FMS respondents predicted 'no landing') has peaked, while fear of a hard landing (6%) is too low.
BofA expects downward revisions to 2027 forecasts of 5% US nominal GDP growth and 45% global tech EPS growth (94% in 2026).
Weekly flows were $140.4bn to cash (7th biggest weekly inflow on record), $89.2bn to stocks, $11.6bn to bonds and $0.1bn to gold, with $1.8bn out of crypto.

Global equities took in $89.2bn, and the past 4 weeks saw a record $265.6bn inflow ($317.1bn to passive). US equities took in $31.7bn, and China took in $34.5bn, with a record $85.9bn over 4 weeks attributed to 'national team' buying. Europe equities saw outflows.
Tech funds took in $9.8bn, and $44.6bn over 4 weeks is the biggest since July 2026. EM debt had a $6.1bn outflow, the 6th biggest on record and the first since July 2026.

The BofA Bull & Bear Indicator rose to 7.2 from 7.1, signal Neutral. Equity flow is at the 95th percentile and FMS positioning at the 100th percentile (very bullish), while global stock index breadth is at the 21st percentile (bearish).

The BofA Global Breadth Rule shows net 16% of global equity indices oversold. A buy signal needs net 88% oversold, which BofA says requires SPX below 7323 and UK/European indices down another 3-4%. SOX is 17% below its 200-day moving average, and 20-25% below is a good entry point since 1996.
The FMS Cash Indicator at 3.9% gives a Sell signal, and the EM Flow Trading Rule at 4.3% also gives a Sell.

BofA private clients hold 65.8% stocks (3-month low), 17.7% bonds (7-month high) and 9.3% cash (record low). They bought TIPS, bank loan and muni bond ETFs and sold EM debt, staples and utilities ETFs.
Year-to-date returns as of Nov 4, 2026: oil +58.8% (per headline; Table 6 shows 53.5%), global stocks +8.8%, US stocks +7.4%, gold -5.3%, bitcoin -13.0%.
Polymarket odds for the 2028 election: Democrats 68%, Republicans 31%. Ossoff leads the Democratic nomination at 28% and Vance leads the Republican nomination at 35%.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscaler capex consensus is $820bn in 2026 and $1.3tn in 2027. The case for a bubble rests on AI compared to railroads, US government backstop of AI, and the buy-the-dip habit of Gen Z and Gen X.
tension_points.bear_case: Free cash flow turns to -$63bn in 2026 and -$252bn in 2027. Debt and equity issuance is surging, bond markets want slower capex, and data centers are electorally unpopular.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Bond yields resetting lower without a recession would bring AI stocks back into favour, but at a slower build pace with more regulation and taxes.

tension_points.bull_case: If inflation falls and the tightening cycle ends before a credit event or recession, 2027 stays goldilocks with bullish breadth.
tension_points.bear_case: Another Fed hike on Dec 9 (64%) alongside ECB, BOE and BOJ hikes keeps financial conditions tight while oil stays high.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Weak November CPI and payrolls would mean the December hikes are the last. Oil below $80/bbl and 10-year UST yield below 4.5% would reverse the tightening of financial conditions.

tension_points.bull_case: With recession odds low (banks IXG hold $125, mid-caps MDY $666, junk bonds JNK $92), SPX holds above 7,000 and risk rotates.
tension_points.bear_case: The SPW double-top and a 15% one-month NDX decline with tech leaders broken signal a larger top.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Banks IXG below $125, mid-caps MDY below $666 or junk bonds JNK below $92 would signal rising recession odds.
